CHIEF COMPLAINT
Joint pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 62-year-old male with a past medical history of kidney transplant, hypothyroidism, and arthritis who presents with bilateral knee pain. The pain began over the weekend while the patient was moving boxes up and down basement stairs. He describes the pain as equally affecting both knees and attributes it to the repetitive activity and weight of the boxes, though he notes a history of prior knee problems. The pain was severe enough to disturb his sleep on Saturday night. He has attempted conservative management with acetaminophen and ice without significant relief. The patient denies any specific traumatic injury.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or headaches. Reports occasional baseline elbow pain. No other acute symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Kidney transplant (performed a few years ago for polycystic kidney disease)
Hypothyroidism
Arthritis
History of knee problems

MEDICATIONS
Immunosuppressive medications
Synthroid

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Active lifestyle; recently engaged in moving activities over the weekend.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Normal, afebrile, normal heart rate and blood pressure
Cardiac: 2/6 systolic ejection murmur noted, stable compared to prior exams
Right knee: Edema and erythema present, pain to palpation, decreased range of motion
Left knee: Appears normal
Remainder of exam: Unremarkable

RESULTS
Right knee X-ray: Good bony alignment, no acute fracture
Laboratory studies: White blood cell count not elevated, kidney function very good

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute exacerbation of arthritis/bilateral knee pain
   - Prescribed Ultram 50 mg every 6 hours as needed
   - Ordered autoimmune panel
   - Advised to rest and take it easy
   - Will consider further imaging and physical therapy referral if symptoms persist over next couple of weeks

2. Hypothyroidism
   - Continue current Synthroid therapy
   - Ordered thyroid panel

3. Chronic arthritis
   - Continue current management
   - Limited options for anti-inflammatory medications due to kidney transplant status
   - Follow-up in a couple of weeks; will consider physical therapy referral if needed
